page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It features a constrained compute footprint of 2 vCPUs derived from 1 dedicated physical core with 2 threads, paired with 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 32.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a high memory density of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent with a zero GPU count, but the configuration includes 161 GB of local SSD storage alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage.

Benchmark results highlight an asymmetry between single-threaded capabilities and total throughput. Single-core evaluations reveal moderate performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1630.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 1890.49, both placing within the middle 50% tier. Instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions enable stable execution in single-stream tasks like gzip compression (28.34 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (10.19 GB/sec). However, overall multi-core performance is limited by the single-core topology, resulting in bottom-decile scores across multi-core stress-ng (1933.27), Geekbench multi-core (1878.0), and PassMark CPU (2986.1).

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate 104.76 GB/sec for small cached reads, falling to 14.31 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 13.48 GB/sec for large writes. Application benchmarks mirror the restricted core count, with Redis recording 2.02 million SET operations per second and static web serving achieving 3.53 GB/sec throughput, both falling into lower percentiles. The E4-2ds_v5 provides a cost-effective allocation of substantial memory without requiring the purchase of unneeded compute cores, though it exhibits severe throughput tradeoffs in compute-bound parallel processing.

The instance is appropriately aligned with workloads requiring significant memory capacity and fast scratch space without concurrent compute demands. Primary use cases include small in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, lightweight enterprise applications, staging environments, and single-threaded data transformation jobs.
